chunks: My father - may God be pleased with him - narrated that Sa'd ibn Abdullah narrated to me that Muhammad ibn Isa, from Abbas (ibn Hilal al-Shami) - the servant of Al-Ridha (peace be upon him), from Abu al-Hasan Al-Ridha (peace be upon him) said: I heard him saying:

Whoever says when he hears the call to the morning prayer: 'O God! I ask You by the approach of Your day and the departure of Your night, and the presence of Your prayers and the voices of Your supplications, that You send blessings upon Muhammad and the family of Muhammad and that You forgive me, for You are the Oft-Returning, the Merciful' - and similarly when he hears the call to the evening prayer, then dies on that day or that night, dies having repented [enters Paradise].
ai.seo_question: What is the reward for reciting a specific supplication after hearing the morning or evening call to prayer?
ai.summary: Recorded by Shaykh al-Saduq in *Uyun Akhbar al-Rida*, this hadith highlights the spiritual potency of aligning one's supplication with the transitional moments of the Adhan, specifically invoking Allah’s attributes of Acceptance (*Iqbal*) and Forgiveness (*Tawwab*). The promise of dying in a state of repentance (*Tawab*) upon reciting this du'a and passing away that same day underscores the Shia emphasis on the immediacy of divine mercy and the efficacy of specific, prophetic supplications in securing a favorable end (*Husn al-Khatimah*).

en.dr-ali-peiravi: 26-1 (The author of the book narrated) my father - may God be pleased with him - narrated that Sa’d ibn Abdullah quoted on the authority of Muhammad ibn Isa, on the authority of Abbas (ibn Hilal al-Shami) - the servant of Al-Ridha (s), “I heard Al-Ridha (s) say, ‘

Whoever says the following supplication when he hears the morning or evening call toprayer and dies on that day or night has died having repented (and will enter Paradise): O my God! I ask Thee on behalf of Thy morning and Thy night, and the voice of Thy callers that You send Blessings upon Muhammad and his Household and that You forgive me as Thee are the Forgiver, the Merciful.’”
